summary.text: Matthew Dunlap is the Democratic nominee for Maine's 2nd Congressional District and the sitting Maine State Auditor. A former journalist and columnist, he served in the Maine House, as Secretary of State in two separate stretches, and ran for U.S. Senate in 2012; he won the 2026 Democratic primary after a ranked-choice runoff.

paragraphs.text: Dunlap was born and raised in Bar Harbor, Maine, and graduated from Mount Desert Island High School.

He earned a bachelor's degree in history in 1987 and a master's degree in English literature in 1994 from the University of Maine, and also completed Harvard University's Senior Executives in State and Local Government program.

Dunlap worked for 25 years as a journalist and columnist for The Northwoods Sporting Journal and other publications, and for nearly a year as executive director of the Sportsman's Alliance of Maine. He has also worked in commercial food service, nonprofit administration, textiles, and farming.
Dunlap served in the Maine House of Representatives from 1996 to 2004, representing Old Town (District 121), and chaired the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife.

The Legislature elected him Maine Secretary of State in 2004, and he served from 2005 to 2011; he was selected again in 2012 and served from 2013 to 2021. He was president of the National Association of Secretaries of State from 2010 to 2011.
In 2012 he finished second in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, behind Cynthia Dill.
The Legislature elected Dunlap State Auditor in December 2020; he served briefly in 2021 and was selected again on November 14, 2022.

He announced a Democratic primary challenge to Rep. Jared Golden in October 2025, and Golden announced in November 2025 that he would not seek re-election. Dunlap won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary in a ranked-choice runoff.

Dunlap is a founding board member of the Maine Youth Fish and Game Association and a past member of the University of Maine Board of Visitors and the Bangor Symphony Orchestra board. He lives in Old Town, Maine.
